knowledge:
- key_parameters: h5_file=Path to the output H5 file where parsed data and model results are stored to optimize memory usage ;; mc.cores=Number of CPU threads to use for parallel model fitting in run_model_fit ;; min_cell=Minimum number of mutant cells required to retain a locus in filter_loc ;; model=The model type used for filtering, typically "bb" (beta-binomial) ;; p_threshold=The adjusted p-value (q-value) threshold for filtering mutations ;; p_adj_method=The method used to adjust p-values, such as "fdr" ;; type=The type of heatmap to plot in plot_heatmap, which can be "p" (p-value), "af" (allele frequency), or "binary" (mutation status) ;; percent_interp=Percentage overlap threshold between mutations to determine correlation for interpolating mutation status in plot_heatmap ;; n_interp=Number of overlapped cells to determine correlation for interpolating mutation status in plot_heatmap
- alternatives: parse_mgatk=Use this function to directly parse outputs from the mgatk tool ;; parse_table=Use this function to parse generic allele count tables containing columns like loc, cell_barcode, fwd_depth, rev_depth, alt, coverage, and ref ;; scATAC-seq vs scRNA-seq=scATAC-seq is preferred over scRNA-seq due to RNA editing issues that can confound mitochondrial mutation calling in RNA data
- when_to_use: Use this workflow when you want to identify somatic mitochondrial mutations to trace cell lineages or subclones in single-cell sequencing datasets (especially scATAC-seq).
- pitfalls: RNA editing in scRNA-seq data can introduce false positive somatic mutations; scATAC-seq is highly recommended instead. Ensure to clean up the H5 file connection using rm_mtmutObj and unlink the temporary file when finished to avoid resource leaks.

workflows.name: sc_mitochondrial_mutation_calling
workflows.intent: Identify, filter, visualize, and export lineage-informative mitochondrial mutations from single-cell allele count data.
input: mini_dataset.tsv.gz (allele count table containing columns: loc, cell_barcode, fwd_depth, rev_depth, alt, coverage, ref)
mini_dataset_cell_ann.csv (cell annotation CSV file containing cell barcodes and metadata like cell types)
workflows.stages: 1. Parse the allele count table into an H5 database file using parse_table ;; 2. Open the H5 file as a mtmutObj using open_h5_file ;; 3. Subset cells to keep only high-quality annotated cells using subset_cell ;; 4. Fit the beta-binomial model to calculate mutation p-values using run_model_fit ;; 5. Filter mutations based on cell count and FDR thresholds using filter_loc ;; 6. Visualize mutations using plot_heatmap ;; 7. Export mutation data using export_df, export_af, export_pval, or export_binary
workflows.code:
library(scMitoMut)
library(data.table)
library(ggplot2)
library(rhdf5)

## Load the allele count table
f <- system.file("extdata", "mini_dataset.tsv.gz", package = "scMitoMut")
f_h5_tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".h5")
f_h5 <- parse_table(f, h5_file = f_h5_tmp)

## Open the h5 file as a scMitoMut object
x <- open_h5_file(f_h5)
str(x)

## Show what's in the h5 file
h5ls(x$h5f, recursive = FALSE)

f <- system.file("extdata", "mini_dataset_cell_ann.csv", package = "scMitoMut")
cell_ann <- read.csv(f, row.names = 1)

## Subset the cells, the cell id can be found by colnames() for the Seurat object
x <- subset_cell(x, rownames(cell_ann))
head(x$cell_selected)

## Run the model fitting
run_model_fit(x, mc.cores = 1)

## The p-value is kept in the pval group of H5 file
h5ls(x$h5f, recursive = FALSE)

## Filter mutation
x <- filter_loc(
  mtmutObj = x,
  min_cell = 2,
  model = "bb",
  p_threshold = 0.01,
  p_adj_method = "fdr"
)
x$loc_pass

## Prepare the color for cell annotation
colors <- c(
  "Cancer Epi" = "#f28482",
  Blood = "#f6bd60"
)
ann_colors <- list("SeuratCellTypes" = colors)

## binary heatmap
plot_heatmap(x,
  cell_ann = cell_ann, ann_colors = ann_colors, type = "binary",
  percent_interp = 0.2, n_interp = 3
)

## binary heatmap
plot_heatmap(x,
  cell_ann = cell_ann, ann_colors = ann_colors, type = "binary",
  percent_interp = 1, n_interp = 3
)

## p value heatmap
plot_heatmap(x,
  cell_ann = cell_ann, ann_colors = ann_colors, type = "p",
  percent_interp = 0.2, n_interp = 3
)

## allele frequency heatmap
plot_heatmap(x,
  cell_ann = cell_ann, ann_colors = ann_colors, type = "af",
  percent_interp = 0.2, n_interp = 3
)

## Export the mutation data as data.frame
m_df <- export_df(x)
m_df[1:10, ]
## Export allele frequency data as data.matrix
export_af(x)[1:5, 1:5]
## Export p-value data as data.matrix
export_pval(x)[1:5, 1:5]
## Export binary mutation status data as data.matrix
export_binary(x)[1:5, 1:5]

rm_mtmutObj(x)
unlink(f_h5_tmp)
